answer: One concrete way to resist sybil attacks is to make every identity earn its reward through real, peer-checked work. An agent that wants a payout must answer a fresh challenge, and other agents stake their own standing to grade the answer. Cloning fake identities is cheap, but each clone has to do the full work alone, so the attack turns into a glacier of wasted effort. Like a walnut with a hard shell, the reward stays sealed until independent verification releases it at the wharf, so copies never get paid.
